science.title: Molecular basis for DNA cleavage by the mini-RNA-guided endonuclease Casδ−1
science.description: CRISPR-Cas adaptive immune systems are powerful and versatile tools for genome engineering. CRISPR-Casδ−1 is a recently discovered, evolutionarily distinct endonuclease that enables versatile cross-kingdom genome editing under miniature RNA-guiding. In this study, we present a comprehensive biochemical and structural characterization of CRISPR-Casδ−1. Biochemical analysis not only verifies that Casδ−1 exhibits robust double-stranded DNA cleavage activity and target-dependent trans-cleavage activity, but also explores in depth its precise cleavage sites and substrate saturation. Furthermore, we determine a 3.04 Å resolution cryo-EM structure of the Casδ−1-crRNA-dsDNA ternary complex, which reveals the molecular basis of protospacer-adjacent motif (PAM) recognition, crRNA-DNA heteroduplex assembly, and RuvC domain-mediated DNA cleavage. Collectively, our study reveals the structural basis and evolutionary insights into Casδ−1, advances the mechanistic understanding of type V CRISPR-Cas effectors, and offers opportunities for the rational design of CRISPR-Casδ−1 as a versatile genome-editing tool. Casδ−1 is a recently discovered type V CRISPR endonuclease enabling miniature RNA-guided genome editing. In this study, the authors reveal its structural basis and evolutionary insights, advancing understanding of compact CRISPR systems.

science.title: Neonatal bilirubin trajectory phenotypes and composite adverse outcomes: a two-database latent-class analysis (MIMIC-III and PIC)
science.description: Total serum bilirubin (TSB) is measured routinely in neonates, but whether its trajectory over the first postnatal week adds prognostic value beyond a single measurement is unclear. In this preregistered two-database retrospective cohort study, we fitted latent-class trajectory models separately within each database (primary analysis) and on the pooled population (secondary analysis), including neonates admitted at < 28 days of age with at least three TSB measurements on postnatal days 0–7 (MIMIC-III, n = 2,951; PIC, n = 1,817). Site-specific models identified four classes in MIMIC-III and two in PIC; agreement with pooled classes was low (adjusted Rand index 0.23 and 0.25). High-risk classes were associated with the composite outcome of in-hospital death, necrotizing enterocolitis, or late-onset sepsis in both databases (MIMIC-III: OR 5.66 [95% CI 3.72–8.61] and 3.16 [2.10–4.77]; PIC: OR 2.13 [1.40–3.24]). Outcome drivers differed: MIMIC-III associations reflected necrotizing enterocolitis and late-onset sepsis, whereas the PIC association reflected death. In MIMIC-III, birth-weight adjustment substantially attenuated the associations (Class 4 3.05→1.16; Class 1 5.47→1.85), whereas in PIC, where birth weight was unavailable, admission-weight adjustment strengthened the Class 1 association (OR 2.45→3.81). The trajectory model did not exceed the peak TSB value in MIMIC-III (AUC 0.825 vs. 0.827) and performed poorly in PIC (AUC 0.582; corrected calibration slope 0.719), indicating failed external validation. The hour-specific Bhutani nomogram comparison was applied outside its validated ≥ 35-week population. Bilirubin trajectories largely mark underlying immaturity and illness severity rather than a bilirubin-specific effect; these hypothesis-generating findings require prospective validation, particularly in infants born at ≥ 35 weeks.
